anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer chooses a substantially sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are adequate.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Critical engine parameters (memory, parallelism, checkpointing, etc.) are mis-aligned with hardware and workload characteristics.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Total memory consumed by caches, work areas, and background structures grows beyond safe host capacity.

When all three conditions are present simultaneously, the system exhibits a blend of erratic plan changes, parameter-driven resource imbalance, and escalating memory pressure. Symptoms may include: plans oscillating between parallel full scans and single-threaded index access as the cost model reacts to shifting memory availability; sudden bursts of hash or sort memory that push the instance into paging, followed by emergency re-planning; CPU cores alternately over- and under-utilized because mis-set parallelism caps clash with the optimizer’s plan choices; checkpoint or log-flush storms triggered when inflated buffer pools contend with swap activity; and highly variable response times where the same statement alternates between milliseconds and minutes.

Causal chain: mis-tuned configuration parameters (e.g., oversized work memory, aggressive parallel-worker limits, or an over-grown buffer pool) permit individual queries to claim far more memory than the host can supply. The optimizer, unaware of real-time OS pressure, may favor memory-intensive hash joins or large parallel plans—amplifying consumption initiated by the configuration mistake. As memory saturates, the operating system begins paging, which slows I/O, disrupts feedback loops, and triggers re-optimizations that may select even less efficient plans. The resulting vicious cycle—bad parameters enabling greedy plans, greedy plans exhausting memory, and memory pressure provoking further unstable plan selection—magnifies latency, throughput variability, and the risk of OOM termination.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that takes more than the specified amount of time; zero disables the timeout.
entry.trigger_condition: A SQL statement runs longer than statement_timeout, measured from command arrival until completion.
entry.workload_impact: The running statement is aborted; when configured, the timed-out statement is logged.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
